results.title: Strict total order
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A strict total order on a type $\alpha$ consists of a binary relation $<$ on $\alpha$ that is irreflexive (no $a < a$), transitive ($a < b$ and $b < c$ imply $a < c$) and total on distinct elements (if $a \ne b$, then $a < b$ or $b < a$). It models strict preference.

results.title: Strict total orders are determined by their relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two strict total orders on a type $\alpha$ with the same relation are equal.

path: Dual groups of finite abelian groups

results.title: A finite abelian group is isomorphic to its dual group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite abelian group $A$ is isomorphic to its dual group, the group of characters of $A$ under pointwise multiplication, where a character of $A$ is a map $\chi : A \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\chi(0) = 1$ and $\chi(a + a') = \chi(a)\chi(a')$ for all $a, a' \in A$.

results.title: Characters of a product of abelian groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all abelian groups $A$ and $B$, the group of characters of $A \times B$ is isomorphic to the product of the character groups of $A$ and $B$. Here a character of $A$ is a map $\chi : A \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\chi(0) = 1$ and $\chi(a + a') = \chi(a)\chi(a')$ for all $a, a' \in A$, and the characters of $A$ form a group under pointwise multiplication.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 19.20 (Cameron)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that every finite group $G$ with $|\mathrm{End}(G)| = |\mathrm{PIso}(G)|$ is abelian. Here $\mathrm{End}(G)$ is the set of endomorphisms of $G$, and $\mathrm{PIso}(G)$ is the set of partial isomorphisms of $G$: the triples $(H, K, f)$ of subgroups $H$, $K$ of $G$ and an isomorphism $f \colon H \to K$.

results.title: Equal endomorphism and partial isomorphism counts do not force commutativity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finite non-abelian group $G$ with $|\mathrm{End}(G)| = |\mathrm{PIso}(G)|$. Here $\mathrm{End}(G)$ is the set of endomorphisms of $G$, and $\mathrm{PIso}(G)$ is the set of partial isomorphisms of $G$: the triples $(H, K, f)$ of subgroups $H$, $K$ of $G$ and an isomorphism $f \colon H \to K$. This answers Kourovka Problem 19.20 (P. J. Cameron) in the negative.

results.title: A preconnected set meets the frontier of every set it crosses
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ be a preconnected subset of a topological space $X$ and let $A \subseteq X$. If both $s \cap A$ and $s \cap (X \setminus A)$ are nonempty, then $s$ meets the frontier $\partial A = \overline{A} \setminus \operatorname{int} A$ of $A$, that is, $s \cap \partial A$ is nonempty.

results.title: Rouché's theorem on a disc
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c \in \mathbb{C}$ and $R > 0$, and let $f$ and $g$ be analytic at every point of the closed disc $|z - c| \le R$. If $|g(z)| < |f(z)|$ for every $z$ on the circle $|z - c| = R$, then $f$ and $f + g$ have the same number of zeros in the open disc $|z - c| < R$, counted with multiplicity: the divisors of $f$ and of $f + g$ on the open disc have equal sums.

results.title: Approximation property
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A normed space has the approximation property if, on every compact set, the identity operator is a uniform limit of finite-rank continuous linear operators.

results.title: Finite-dimensional spaces have the approximation property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Finite-dimensional spaces have the approximation property: the identity operator is itself finite-rank.

results.title: Banach spaces with a Schauder basis have the approximation property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A Banach space with a Schauder basis has the approximation property. The partial-sum projections are finite-rank, converge pointwise to the identity, and are uniformly bounded by the Banach–Steinhaus theorem (`SchauderBasis.exists_norm_proj_le`); pointwise convergence plus uniform boundedness gives uniform convergence on compact sets via a finite `ε`-net argument.

results.title: Approximation property is invariant under linear isomorphism
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Approximation property passes to complemented subspaces
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The approximation property passes to complemented subspaces: if `P` is a continuous projection onto the submodule `F`, restrict a finite-rank approximant on the ambient space via `P`. The key point is that `P` fixes every point of `F`, so `P (S x) - x = P (S x - x)` for `x ∈ F`.

results.title: Separable Hilbert spaces have the approximation property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A Hilbert space with a Hilbert basis indexed by `ℕ` has the approximation property, via the associated Schauder basis (`HilbertBasis.toSchauderBasis`).

results.title: Accepting transformations of a DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a DFA $M$ with set of states $Q$, start state $q_0$ and accepting states $F$, the accepting transformations of $M$ are the state transformations $f$ of $Q$ with $f(q_0) \in F$.

results.title: The transition morphism recognizes through accepting transformations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with start state $q_0$ and accepting states $F$. The transition morphism of $M$, from words to state transformations, recognizes the language accepted by $M$ through the accepting transformations of $M$: a word is accepted by $M$ exactly when the transformation it induces sends $q_0$ into $F$.

results.title: The transition monoid recognizes the accepted language
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with start state $q_0$ and accepting states $F$. The map sending each word to the element of the transition monoid of $M$ that it induces recognizes the language accepted by $M$, with accepting set the elements $f$ of the transition monoid such that $f(q_0) \in F$: a word is accepted by $M$ exactly when the transformation it induces sends $q_0$ into $F$.

results.title: Finitely many state transformations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $Q$ is a finite set, then the monoid of state transformations of $Q$, consisting of all functions $Q \to Q$ multiplied in diagrammatic order, is finite.

results.title: Transition monoids of finite automata are finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every DFA $M$ with a finite set of states, the transition monoid of $M$ is finite.

results.title: Regular languages have finite syntactic monoids
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $L$ is a regular language, then the syntactic monoid of $L$ is finite.

results.title: Regular languages are those with finite syntactic monoid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A language $L$ is regular if and only if the syntactic monoid of $L$ is finite.

results.title: The transition monoid maps to the syntactic monoid
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a DFA $M$ accepting the language $L$, this is the monoid homomorphism from the transition monoid of $M$ to the syntactic monoid of $L$ that sends the transformation induced by each word $w$ to the syntactic class of $w$.

results.title: Johnson's algorithm fails exactly on reachable negative cycles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $E$ of directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with integer weights, Johnson's algorithm on $E$ returns no table if and only if there is a vertex $s$ from which a negative cycle of $E$ is reachable.

results.title: Correctness of Johnson's algorithm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with integer weights, and suppose Johnson's algorithm on $E$ returns a table $d$. Then for all vertices $s$ and $t$, $d(s, t) = \infty$ if and only if $t$ is not reachable from $s$ along edges of $E$. Moreover, if $d(s, t)$ is an integer $x$, then some weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $t$ has weight $x$, and every weighted path in $E$ from $s$…

results.title: Exact cost of a successful run of Johnson's algorithm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of $m$ directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with integer weights. If Johnson's algorithm on $E$ returns a table, then its counted cost is exactly $n^3 + nm + (n+1)(m+n) + 2n^2 + 4m + 5n + 1$.

results.title: Cost bound for Johnson's algorithm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $E$ of $m$ directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with integer weights, the counted cost of Johnson's algorithm on $E$, including the case where it extracts a negative cycle, is at most $n^3 + nm + (n+1)(m+n) + 2n^2 + 4m + 5n + 1 + 3(n+1)$.

results.title: Greedy choice of a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list $F$ of finite sets and a finite set $U$, the best set of $F$ for $U$ is the first set $S$ in the list $F$ that maximizes $|S \cap U|$, or $\emptyset$ when $F$ is empty.

results.title: Greedy set cover
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F = [S_1, \dots, S_n]$ be a list of finite sets and $U$ a finite set. The greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ is computed as follows. Let $T$ be the first $S_i$ in the list that maximizes $|S_i \cap U|$, or $T = \emptyset$ when $n = 0$. If $T \cap U = \emptyset$, the result is the empty list; otherwise it is $T$ followed by the greedy set cover of $U \setminus T$ from $F$. Each step, including the last one, costs…

results.title: The greedy set cover draws its sets from the family
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $F$ of finite sets and every finite set $U$, every set in the list returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ is a member of $F$.

results.title: The greedy set cover is a cover
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets and $U$ a finite set such that every element of $U$ lies in some set of $F$. Then every element of $U$ lies in some set of the list returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$.

results.title: The greedy set cover has at most as many sets as elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $F$ of finite sets and every finite set $U$, the list returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $|U|$.

results.title: Running time of greedy set cover
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets and $U$ a finite set. The running time of greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ is at most $(|U| + 1)(|F| + \sum_{S \in F} |S|)$, where $|F|$ is the length of the list and the sum runs over the entries of $F$, counted with repetition.

results.title: Lower bound for a difference of harmonic numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $H(n) = 1 + \frac12 + \dots + \frac1n$ for the $n$-th harmonic number, so $H(0) = 0$. For natural numbers $d \le a \le k$, we have $\frac{d}{k} \le H(a) - H(a - d)$, where $\frac{d}{k}$ is read as $0$ when $k = 0$.

results.title: Covering bound by intersections
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a list of finite sets and $T$ a finite set such that every element of $T$ lies in some member of $L$. Then $|T| \le \sum_{S \in L} |S \cap T|$, where the sum runs over the list $L$ with repetitions.

results.title: Potential bound for greedy set cover
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set, and $H(n) = 1 + \frac12 + \dots + \frac1n$ the $n$-th harmonic number. For every list $C^*$ of members of $F$ that together cover $U$, the list of sets returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $\sum_{S \in C^*} H(|S \cap U|)$, where the sum runs over the list $C^*$ with repetitions.

results.title: Harmonic bound in the largest set size for greedy set cover
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets each with at most $d$ elements, $U$ a finite set, and $H(n) = 1 + \frac12 + \dots + \frac1n$ the $n$-th harmonic number. For every list $C^*$ of members of $F$ that together cover $U$, the list of sets returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $|C^*| \cdot H(d)$, where $|C^*|$ is the length of $C^*$.

results.title: Harmonic bound in the universe size for greedy set cover
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set, and $H(n) = 1 + \frac12 + \dots + \frac1n$ the $n$-th harmonic number. For every list $C^*$ of members of $F$ that together cover $U$, the list of sets returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $|C^*| \cdot H(|U|)$, where $|C^*|$ is the length of $C^*$.

results.title: Greedy set cover is a logarithmic approximation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets and $U$ a finite set. For every list $C^*$ of members of $F$ that together cover $U$, the list of sets returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $|C^*| \cdot (\ln |U| + 1)$, where $|C^*|$ is the length of $C^*$ and $\ln 0 = 0$.

results.title: Set with the least cost per new element
results.caption: Definition

results.summary: For every list $F$ of finite sets, finite set $U$ and rational cost function $w$ on finite sets, every set chosen by the weighted greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ with costs $w$ belongs to $F$.

results.title: The weighted greedy set cover is a cover
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set and $w$ any rational cost function on finite sets. If every element of $U$ lies in some set of $F$, then every element of $U$ lies in some set chosen by the weighted greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ with costs $w$.

results.title: Running time of weighted greedy set cover
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Total cost of a list of sets

results.summary: Let $S$ and $M$ be finite sets of natural numbers. $M$ contains a homothetic copy of $S$ if there are a natural number $a > 0$ and an integer $b$ such that $as + b \in M$ for every $s \in S$, that is, $aS + b \subseteq M$. This is Maker's winning condition.

results.title: Copies of finite sets of rationals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets of rational numbers. $B$ is a copy of $A$ if there are rationals $a > 0$ and $b$ such that $B = aA + b = \{ax + b : x \in A\}$.

results.title: Reflections of finite sets of rationals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets of rational numbers. $B$ is a reflection of $A$ if there are rationals $a < 0$ and $b$ such that $B = aA + b = \{ax + b : x \in A\}$.

results.title: Symmetric sets of a given type
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $S = \{s_0 < s_1 < \dots < s_{n-1}\}$ be a finite set of $n$ rational numbers and let $i, j < n$. Then $S$ is called symmetric of type $(i, j)$ if $i < j$ and $S \setminus \{s_i\}$ is a copy of $S \setminus \{s_j\}$.

results.title: Symmetric sets of rationals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $S$ of rational numbers is symmetric if it is symmetric of some type $(i, j)$ with $i, j < |S|$.

results.title: The zero-geometric set $S_2(n, k)$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a rational number $k$, $S_2(n, k)$ is the finite set of rationals $\{0\} \cup \{k^i : 0 \le i < n - 1\}$, that is, $\{0, 1, k, \dots, k^{n-2}\}$ when $n \ge 2$ and $\{0\}$ when $n \le 1$.

results.title: Winning within zero moves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers, and let $M$ and $B$ be finite sets of natural numbers. Maker wins the $S$-game within $0$ moves from the position where Maker has claimed $M$ and Breaker has claimed $B$ if and only if $M$ contains a copy $aS + b = \{as + b : s \in S\}$ of $S$, where $a$ is a positive integer and $b$ is an integer.
